issues.body: Section 5 still claims that publishing the new base before deleting folded shards makes every record visible at least once to any interleaving. A reader that fetches the old base first, then lists the tail after publication and deletion, sees the record in neither source. The later 404/base-re-fetch rule only helps when the reader previously listed the deleted shard; it cannot detect an already-empty newer listing.
issues.fix_hint: Qualify the at-least-once claim and make reader operation ordering or a generation/manifest validation part of the future protocol obligation. For example, specify a read order plus a generation check across base and tail, retrying or failing closed whenever the generation changes.
issues.title: Publish-before-delete still does not cover every reader ordering

verdict.summary: The round-2 minor finding remains unchanged. The protocol sketch still says publish-before-delete makes every record visible at least once to any reader interleaving, but a reader can fetch the old base before publication and list the tail after deletion, observing neither copy. The later stale-listing/404 rule cannot detect that ordering. This remains non-blocking because the record repeatedly and explicitly treats Option B's protocol as incomplete, unreviewed, and a condition that must be discharged before adoption; no behavior or trust-plane control changes ship in this design-only diff.
